newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel sellers bullish, see demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel sellers bullish, see demand.

text.p: Low sulphur straight-run markets were bullish on Wednesday, with seller confidence picking up on perceived buyer demand, traders said.
After Tuesday's $94.75 fob deal offer numbers picked up, with sellers starting their negotiations at around $100 fob.
A solid $104 cif bid was registered in Britain, though it was not clear by close of business whether a deal had been closed.
A cargo was rumoured sold out of northern Germany late on Tuesday for trans-atlantic delivery but details were hard to pin down.
"There is definetly more interest in straight-run, with margins on running it beginning to look more favourable vis a vis crude," one seller said.
In the Mediterranean buyers were not convinced, still preferring to process crude, and Black Sea straight-runs were considered unattractive.
Two or three M-40 cargoes were reported available in Odessa and Novorossisk in the first decade of May.
In the north two M-100s that were sold yesterday were reported to have gone for a healthy two means + $6 and +$6.50.
